headline: Hi-Tech Gears Limited enters Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
sum: Hi-Tech Gears Limited has been admitted into Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, as intimated to NSE on 20 August 2026.
implication: Admission to CIRP triggers a 180-day (extendable to 330-day) moratorium on creditor action; all existing management is superseded by an Interim Resolution Professional, and the company's equity becomes subordinate to secured and operational creditor claims in any resolution or liquidation outcome.
detail: Hi-Tech Gears Limited, an industrial manufacturing entity, has been formally admitted into the CIRP regime following a petition (likely by a financial creditor or operational creditor under IBC s. 7, 9 or 10). The company's admission was disclosed via NSE filing on 20 August 2026. During CIRP, an Interim Resolution Professional assumes control; creditors' claims are verified and admitted by 21 December 2026 (typically); a Resolution Plan is invited and voted upon by the Committee of Creditors within the statutory window. The company's operations remain subject to the RP's discretion and the CoC's oversight.

structure.novel: Standard CIRP mechanics; no novel structure indicated. Admission via exchange intimation suggests either Financial Creditor petition (IBC § 7) or Operational Creditor petition (IBC § 9) with an undisputed debt trigger.

triggers.note: CIRP initiation by Financial Creditor (default/NPA threshold), Operational Creditor (unpaid 300-day+ invoice), or Corporate Debtor (own application); admission order triggers moratorium and RP supersession.
Moratorium: all civil suits, criminal prosecutions, recovery proceedings against the CD are frozen; asset disposals prohibited unless RP-approved.
